mn42:2.5: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’
mn42:2.6: He has realized with his own insight this world—with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, gods and humans—and he makes it known to others.
mn42:2.7: He teaches Dhamma that’s good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased; and he reveals an entirely full and pure spiritual life.
mn42:6.2: Please, worthy Gotama, teach us the Dhamma in such a way that we might understand the detailed meaning of the worthy Gotama’s brief statement.”
mn42:6.3: “Well then, householders, listen and pay close attention, I will speak.”
mn42:6.4: “Yes, sir,” the brahmins and householders of Verañjā replied.
mn42:8.1: And how is a person of unprincipled and immoral conduct threefold by way of body?
mn42:8.2: It’s when someone kills living creatures. They’re violent, bloody-handed, a hardened killer, merciless to living beings.
mn42:8.3: They steal. The wealth or belongings of others … they take with the intention to commit theft.
mn42:8.4: They commit sexual misconduct. Women protected by their mother … with women like that they have relations.
mn42:8.5: This is how a person of unprincipled and immoral conduct is threefold by way of body.
mn42:9.1: And how is a person of unprincipled and immoral conduct fourfold by way of speech?
mn42:9.2: It’s when someone lies. Summoned to a council … they deliberately tell a lie.
mn42:9.3: They backbite. Having heard something in one place, they repeat it in another … they speak words that promote division.
mn42:9.4: They speak harshly. Words that are cruel, nasty … they use speech like that.
mn42:9.5: They talk nonsense. Their speech is untimely … rambling and pointless.
mn42:9.6: This is how a person of unprincipled and immoral conduct is fourfold by way of speech.
mn42:10.1: And how is a person of unprincipled and immoral conduct threefold by way of mind?
mn42:10.2: It’s when someone is covetous … if only it were mine!’
mn42:10.3: They have ill will and malicious intentions: ‘May these sentient beings be killed … or may they not exist at all!’
mn42:10.4: They have wrong view. Their perspective is distorted:
mn42:10.5: ‘There’s no meaning in giving, no meaning in sacrifice … who describe the afterlife after realizing it.’
mn42:10.6: This is how a person of unprincipled and immoral conduct is threefold by way of mind.
mn42:10.7: That’s how unprincipled and immoral conduct is the reason why some sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.
mn42:11.1: Householders, a person of principled and moral conduct is threefold by way of body, fourfold by way of speech, and threefold by way of mind.
mn42:12.1: And how is a person of principled and moral conduct threefold by way of body?
mn42:12.2: It’s when someone gives up killing living creatures. They have laid down the rod and the sword; scrupulous and kind, they live full of sympathy for all living beings.
mn42:12.3: They give up stealing. The wealth or belongings of others … they don’t take with the intention to commit theft.
mn42:12.4: They give up sexual misconduct … with women like that they don’t have relations.
mn42:12.5: This is how a person of principled and moral conduct is threefold by way of body.
mn42:13.1: And how is a person of principled and moral conduct fourfold by way of speech?
mn42:13.2: It’s when someone gives up lying. Summoned to a council … they don’t deliberately tell a lie.
mn42:13.3: They give up backbiting … they speak words that promote harmony.
mn42:13.4: They give up harsh speech … they use speech like that.
mn42:13.5: They give up talking nonsense … they say things at the right time that are reasonable, succinct, and beneficial.
mn42:13.6: This is how a person of principled and moral conduct is fourfold by way of speech.
mn42:14.1: And how is a person of principled and moral conduct threefold by way of mind?
mn42:14.2: It’s when someone is not covetous. They don’t covet the wealth and belongings of others: ‘Oh, if only what belongs to another were mine!’
mn42:14.3: They have a kind heart and loving intentions: ‘May these sentient beings be free of enmity and ill will, untroubled, and may they keep themselves happy!’
mn42:14.4: They have right view. Their perspective is undistorted:
mn42:14.5: ‘There is meaning in giving, meaning in sacrifice … who describe the afterlife after realizing it with their own insight.’
mn42:14.6: This is how a person of principled and moral conduct is threefold by way of mind.
mn42:14.7: That’s how principled and moral conduct is the reason why some sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.

mn42:15.3: it’s possible that, when their body breaks up, after death, they will be reborn in the company of well-to-do aristocrats.
mn42:15.5: Because they have principled and moral conduct.

mn42:44.1: When he had spoken, the brahmins and householders of Verañjā said to the Buddha:
mn42:44.3: It’s as if, worthy Gotama, one were to set upright what was overturned, or reveal what was hidden, or point out the path to someone who was lost, or hold up a lamp in the dark, thinking: ‘Those with eyes will see what’s there.’ Just so the worthy Gotama has made the teaching clear in many ways.
mn42:44.4: We go for refuge to the worthy Gotama, to the teaching, and to the mendicant Saṅgha.
mn42:44.5: From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember us as lay followers who have gone for refuge for life.”
mn42:44.6: The People of Verañjā is finished—the second.
